children: KEC International Ltd has announced that it has a new set of orders worth ₹1,407 crore across Transmission & Distribution, Transportation & Cables Businesses.
In an exchange filing issued on Saturday, November 28, the Mumbai-based infrastructure company said it has secured new orders of ₹1,407 crore across various businesses.

These businesses include Transmission & Distribution (T&D), including orders for 220/110/30 kV substations in Africa. It also bagged an additional order for a 765 kV Transmission line from a private developer in India. The T&D orders in this tranche also include supply of towers, hardware and poles in the Americas.
In the transportation segment, the company has bagged a composite order for doubling of railway tracks and associated civil works in India.
Finally, the company expanded its Cables & Conductors business with various orders in India and the overseas markets.

Vimal Kejriwal, MD & CEO, KEC International Ltd. commented, “In T&D, the significant substation order in Africa, together with the transmission line orders secured earlier, has substantially strengthened our order book and reinforced our presence in the African market. In Transportation, we have secured an order in the conventional railway segment, reflecting early signs of improving market opportunities, while maintaining our selective approach to order intake in this business. With these wins, our YTD order intake stands at ~Rs. 15,000 crores.”

Earlier this month, while speaking to CNBC-TV18, Kejriwal said that the second-half margin expansion would be reliant on the pace at which new orders are converted into revenue and the settlement of cost escalation claims. The Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) firm also added that it is targeting order inflows of around ₹28,000 crore in FY27.

In the quarter that concluded in September, the RPG Group company reported an 81.6% year-on-year drop in consolidated net profit, to ₹29.7 crore in the September quarter from ₹161 crore in the same quarter last year.

Revenue decreased 10.2% to ₹5,468 crore from ₹6,091 crore a year earlier. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) fell 36.9% to ₹271.4 crore from ₹430 crore, while the EBITDA margin contracted to 5% from 7.06%.
The share price of KEC International slumped on Friday's trade, falling over 1.60% intraday, taking the stock price below the ₹300 per piece mark.
The stock price has fallen over 60% this year. The stock, at ₹292, has fallen over 61% from its 52-week high of ₹764.80 per share.

title: KEC International bags new orders worth ₹1,400 crore in T&D and cable segments
